text:
samuel: Hey folks — day 1 networking snag. I can access public sites but my dev container inside WSL2 can't pull from our private registry at 10.12.5.20:5000. Chrome on Windows via bastion RDP can reach it. `docker pull 10.12.5.20:5000/my-image` times out inside WSL. Anyone seen this? :wave:

it-jordan: Welcome! :tada: Usually WSL NAT doesn't forward to the VPN adapter. Can you paste `ip addr` (inside WSL) and `route print` (Windows)? Also which VPN client/version?

samuel: Using CorpVPN 3.0. WSL `ip addr` shows `eth0` 172.28.112.7/20. Windows `route print` has 10.12.0.0 via 172.28.96.1 on vEthernet (WSL).

it-jordan: Two quick tries: 1) run `wsl --shutdown` then restart and reconnect VPN. 2) Add a persistent Windows route (admin): `netsh interface ipv4 add route 10.12.0.0/16 "vEthernet (WSL)" 172.28.96.1` — this forces WSL traffic to the VPN gateway.

ops-zoe: If you prefer not to change host routes, use SSH local port forwarding to reach the registry: `ssh -L 5000:10.12.5.20:5000 user@bastion.internal -N` then `docker pull localhost:5000/my-image` from WSL. Or use a SOCKS proxy: `ssh -D1080 -J user@bastion.internal user@bastion.internal` and `curl --socks5-hostname localhost:1080 http://10.12.5.20/health` works for quick tests.

samuel: Tried `wsl --shutdown` — no dice. The netsh route helped for ~10 minutes then packets stopped. Port-forwarding works for pulling images, thanks.

it-jordan: Sounds like the VPN client updates routes dynamically and WSL's NAT sometimes loses the mapping. I'll escalate to network team; we can either push DNS/routes into the WSL vNIC or recommend ephemeral dev hosts.

samuel: Port-forward is good for now. Please open a ticket and cc me.

provision-bot: Ticket created — IT-4399 "WSL2 -> VPN route instability for new hire" assigned to net-team, priority: medium.

samuel: Thanks all! :thumbsup:
